card.name: Formal wording where casual words could go
card.fires_on: Ordinary linking or auxiliary words (this section, should, been, may, to, they, is) inside formal, clinical or official prose. The next word could be a casual filler, but formal text is expected.

modes.label: Auxiliary verbs in warnings
modes.description: Words like should, been, may or is that lead into a clinical statement or caution.
modes.example: Patients possessing a specific history of light sensitive disease states<< should>> not initiate methoxsalen therapy except

modes.label: Linking words in instructions
modes.description: The word to or they that introduces a purpose or condition in directions.
modes.example: In such circumstances, perform a pelvic examination promptly<< to>> evaluate for possible pelvic infection.

modes.label: Section or system nouns
modes.description: A heading-like noun or article in a description of an archive or system.
modes.example: Legal Decisions Archive This<< section>> contains legal decisions regarding native treaty fishing rights

card.writes: It pushes casual hedges and filler such as maybe, things, basically and worried, and pushes down formal words like utilize, assist and individuals.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in formal clinical text and nudges the model toward casual wording instead of stiff officialese.
